items.stem: What is the key difference between interpretability and explainability?

options.text: Interpretability is a model being understandable by design; explainability is explaining a given model after the fact
options.rationale: Correct: one is intrinsic, the other post-hoc.

options.text: Explainability only applies to linear models
options.rationale: Post-hoc methods target complex black boxes too.

options.text: Interpretability requires no model at all
options.rationale: It still concerns a model, just an understandable one.

items.explanation: Correct: one is intrinsic, the other post-hoc.

items.stem: Which TWO cautions apply to a local explanation such as a single SHAP plot? (Select TWO.)

options.text: It explains one prediction and may not generalise to others
Correlated features can share or mask attribution
options.rationale: Correct: attributions can be unstable under correlation.

options.text: It proves the model is unbiased
options.rationale: An explanation does not establish fairness.

options.text: It replaces the need for global analysis
options.rationale: Local and global views answer different questions.
